title: Jason Cohen on bootstrapping vs. raising money, competitor incentives, and hiring people better than you
summary: Jason Cohen explains why he raised money for WP Engine after two years of bootstrapping, and why dogma on funding is unhelpful. He covers studying competitors' incentives to build a distinct strategy, hiring people better than you, and making consistent decisions, including how building in public forces a stronger strategy.

principles.text: Raise money when market size makes it a logical option, not out of ideology; WP Engine's market proved bigger than expected.
principles.quote: about two years in it became clear that the market was way bigger than I thought it really was an opportunity size that you could raise money for

principles.text: Treat every new company with beginner's mind; past experience only makes a few things easier.
principles.quote: you really have to have beginners mind with each company

principles.text: Study competitors' different constraints and goals; that gap is where a distinct strategy comes from.
principles.quote: they have a different set of things they're solving for different set of constraints different different goals than you that's that's the Genesis of a good strategy

principles.text: Calling competitors dumb or evil blinds you to their real strengths and weakens your strategy.
principles.quote: if your attitude is there dumb or bad then then you are not thinking about where they're strong and good and that's what you need to do

principles.text: A founder's job is to hire people better than themselves in each function, or the company never exceeds your own skill.
principles.quote: you're hiring people that specifically are better than you at that function so that that function becomes better than it currently is

principles.text: Make strategic choices that are consistent with each other (e.g., solo means no 24/7 support burden), or you will burn out.
principles.quote: any decision you make is to me is like that's fine but inconsistent decisions they're not fine you need to pick
